Appendix B • Proofs & Comments

B.10 Tensoriality of the torsion (§6.4)

In this appendix, we prove that the torsion of a connection \(\nabla\), \[ \mathtt{T}(df, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) \coloneqq df\left\lceil \mathcal{V}(\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) \right\rfloor, \qquad \mathcal{V}(\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) \coloneqq \nabla_\mathcal{X} \mathcal{Y} - \nabla_\mathcal{Y} \mathcal{X} - [\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}] \in \Gamma T\mathcal{M}, \] is \(C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\)-linear in its first and second entries, i.e. that for all \(g \in C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\), \(df, dh \in \Gamma T^*\mathcal{M}\) and \(\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}, \mathcal{Z} \in \Gamma T\mathcal{M}\), \begin{align*} \mathtt{T}(g \, df + dh, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) &= g \, \mathtt{T}(df, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) + \mathtt{T}(dh, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}), \\ \mathtt{T}(df, g \, \mathcal{X} + \mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{Y}) &= g \, \mathtt{T}(df, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) + \mathtt{T}(df, \mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{Y}), \end{align*} where, as in Chapter 6, sums and s-multiplications of fields are written in compact notation. We will only need the following facts, all established in the main text:

  1. (a)

    The action of a covector field is \(C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\)-linear in the vector field, \(df\left\lceil g \, \mathcal{X} + \mathcal{Z} \right\rfloor = g \, df\left\lceil \mathcal{X} \right\rfloor + df\left\lceil \mathcal{Z} \right\rfloor\), which holds point-wise by linearity of \((df)_p\), since \((g \, \mathcal{X} + \mathcal{Z})(p) = g(p) \, \mathcal{X}(p) + \mathcal{Z}(p)\).

  2. (b)

    The module operations of \(\Gamma T\mathcal{M}\) and \(\Gamma T^*\mathcal{M}\) act point-wise on the actions: \((g \, \mathcal{X} + \mathcal{Z})\left\lfloor f \right\rceil = g \, \mathcal{X}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil + \mathcal{Z}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil\) and \((g \, df + dh)\left\lceil \mathcal{X} \right\rfloor = g \, df\left\lceil \mathcal{X} \right\rfloor + dh\left\lceil \mathcal{X} \right\rfloor\).

  3. (c)

    A vector field acts \(\mathbb{R}\)-linearly on scalar fields and satisfies the Leibniz rule, \(\mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor g f \right\rceil = \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor g \right\rceil f + g \, \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil\).

  4. (d)

    The connection satisfies property 4, \(\nabla_{g\mathcal{X} + \mathcal{Z}} \mathcal{Y} = g \, \nabla_\mathcal{X} \mathcal{Y} + \nabla_\mathcal{Z} \mathcal{Y}\), property 2, and the product rule \(\nabla_\mathcal{Y}(g \, \mathcal{X}) = \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor g \right\rceil \mathcal{X} + g \, \nabla_\mathcal{Y} \mathcal{X}\).

  • First entry: The vector field \(\mathcal{V}(\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y})\) does not depend on the covector field, so linearity in the first entry is just property (b) of the module \(\Gamma T^*\mathcal{M}\): \begin{align*} \mathtt{T}(g \, df + dh, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) &= (g \, df + dh)\left\lceil \mathcal{V}(\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) \right\rfloor = g \, df\left\lceil \mathcal{V}(\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) \right\rfloor + dh\left\lceil \mathcal{V}(\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) \right\rfloor \\ &= g \, \mathtt{T}(df, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) + \mathtt{T}(dh, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}). \end{align*}

  • Second entry, the commutator: The only term requiring some work is the commutator. Letting \([g \, \mathcal{X} + \mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{Y}]\) act on an arbitrary \(f \in C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\), and using (b) and then (c): \begin{align*} [g \, \mathcal{X} + \mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{Y}]\left\lfloor f \right\rceil &= (g \, \mathcal{X} + \mathcal{Z})\left\lfloor \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil \right\rceil - \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor (g \, \mathcal{X} + \mathcal{Z})\left\lfloor f \right\rceil \right\rceil \\ &= g \, \mathcal{X}\left\lfloor \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil \right\rceil + \mathcal{Z}\left\lfloor \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil \right\rceil - \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor g \, \mathcal{X}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil \right\rceil - \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor \mathcal{Z}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil \right\rceil \\ &= g \, \mathcal{X}\left\lfloor \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil \right\rceil + \mathcal{Z}\left\lfloor \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil \right\rceil - \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor g \right\rceil \mathcal{X}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil - g \, \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor \mathcal{X}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil \right\rceil - \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor \mathcal{Z}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil \right\rceil \\ &= g \, [\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}]\left\lfloor f \right\rceil + [\mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{Y}]\left\lfloor f \right\rceil - \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor g \right\rceil \mathcal{X}\left\lfloor f \right\rceil. \end{align*} Since this holds for every \(f\), and using (b) once more, \[ [g \, \mathcal{X} + \mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{Y}] = g \, [\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}] + [\mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{Y}] - \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor g \right\rceil \mathcal{X}. \] The commutator is therefore not \(C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\)-linear: the last term, involving a derivative of \(g\), spoils it.

  • Second entry, the remaining terms: By (d), the first two terms of \(\mathcal{V}\) give \begin{align*} \nabla_{g\mathcal{X} + \mathcal{Z}} \mathcal{Y} &= g \, \nabla_\mathcal{X} \mathcal{Y} + \nabla_\mathcal{Z} \mathcal{Y}, \\ \nabla_\mathcal{Y}(g \, \mathcal{X} + \mathcal{Z}) &= \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor g \right\rceil \mathcal{X} + g \, \nabla_\mathcal{Y} \mathcal{X} + \nabla_\mathcal{Y} \mathcal{Z}, \end{align*} so that the second one also produces a non-tensorial term, \(\mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor g \right\rceil \mathcal{X}\).

  • Second entry, collecting terms: Putting the three contributions together, \begin{align*} \mathcal{V}(g \, \mathcal{X} + \mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{Y}) &= g \, \nabla_\mathcal{X} \mathcal{Y} + \nabla_\mathcal{Z} \mathcal{Y} - \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor g \right\rceil \mathcal{X} - g \, \nabla_\mathcal{Y} \mathcal{X} - \nabla_\mathcal{Y} \mathcal{Z} - g \, [\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}] - [\mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{Y}] + \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor g \right\rceil \mathcal{X} \\ &= g \, \big( \nabla_\mathcal{X} \mathcal{Y} - \nabla_\mathcal{Y} \mathcal{X} - [\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}] \big) + \big( \nabla_\mathcal{Z} \mathcal{Y} - \nabla_\mathcal{Y} \mathcal{Z} - [\mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{Y}] \big) = g \, \mathcal{V}(\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) + \mathcal{V}(\mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{Y}), \end{align*} where the two non-tensorial terms \(\mp \, \mathcal{Y}\left\lfloor g \right\rceil \mathcal{X}\), one coming from the product rule and the other from the commutator, cancel exactly. Finally, by (a), \[ \mathtt{T}(df, g \, \mathcal{X} + \mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{Y}) = df\left\lceil g \, \mathcal{V}(\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) + \mathcal{V}(\mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{Y}) \right\rfloor = g \, \mathtt{T}(df, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) + \mathtt{T}(df, \mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{Y}). \]

Linearity in the third entry needs no separate proof: since \([\mathcal{Y}, \mathcal{X}] = -[\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}]\), the torsion is antisymmetric in its last two entries, \(\mathtt{T}(df, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) = -\mathtt{T}(df, \mathcal{Y}, \mathcal{X})\), and linearity in the third entry follows from linearity in the second. Hence \(\mathtt{T}\) is a \((1,2)\)-tensor field. \(\square\)
